name: Biochemistry, Cellular and Molecular Biology (BCMB) PhD Program
summary: Multidisciplinary PhD program at the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine. First-year students do research in three different labs, then choose one for their thesis.

deadlines.label: Application deadline
deadlines.note: The application is open from 9/8/2026 to 12/1/2026; no time is given. Every part of the application, including English test scores, must arrive by the deadline.

timeline.interviews: Interview invitations go out by late December or early January. The first round is virtual; applicants who advance are invited to a required second-round interview.
timeline.decisions: Acceptance, waitlist and rejection letters come by email. Admitted students decide by April 15.

english.note: TOEFL or IELTS for international applicants whose native language isn't English; no minimum score is stated. Not needed with a degree from a US institution, current study toward a US degree, or a degree from a country whose official language is English. Scores must arrive before the deadline.

applicationFee.note: One fee covers up to four School of Medicine programs. US citizens and permanent residents who meet the School of Medicine's rules may get a waiver; other applicants are asked to check the School of Medicine's fee and waiver instructions.

documents: Details of any prior research experience
requirements.note: There is no minimum GPA; applications are read as a whole. In 2026 the program admitted 13 of 542 applicants.

funding.note: School of Medicine PhD students get guaranteed support under the PhD union's contract: minimum pay of $52,000 in 2026-27, tuition, and health benefits for eligible students. The FAQ says international students also receive a stipend, full tuition, and health and dental coverage. There is no graduate student housing.

international.note: The university sponsors visas for accepted students. Several places are held for international candidates each year.
